# Learn the Seerah

> Learn the Seerah is a free, browser-based app for learning the life of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and his Companions: through the Seerah Song by Zain Bikha, a Sahaba timeline with stories of the Companions, an Arabic Seerah poem and Seerah books. Made by Ummah Apps. URL: https://seerah.ummahapps.ai/

## What it does

- The front page has a card for each part of the app: The Seerah Song (with the lines learnt and the streak); an Arabic Seerah poem, Manzumat al-Munirah fi Muhimm 'Ilm as-Sirah (مَنْظُومَةُ الْمُنِيرَةِ فِي مُهِمِّ عِلْمِ السِّيرَةِ), a short poem by Shaykh Dr Salih al-Usaymi, as a YouTube playlist; the Sahaba Timeline; and books to read more: When the Moon Split (the full story of the Seerah) and Shama’il at-Tirmidhi (the Prophet’s character and appearance, peace be upon him), as PDF downloads.
- The Seerah Song page has today’s practice, the choruses to repeat, the 10 sections and the whole song.
- Plays the song line by line, section by section, or as a whole.
- Repeat a line as many times as you like, or slow it down.
- Follow the lyrics and star each line you learn. Stars are saved in the browser on your device.
- Free, with no sign-up.

## Sahaba Timeline

- At https://seerah.ummahapps.ai/sahaba/
- The lives of the Companions of the Prophet, peace be upon him, side by side on one timeline, in the order they became Muslim, with a dot on each line where that person became Muslim (a dashed dot when the year is not sure, and no dot for those who were children then). Tap a colour in the key to see only that group, and hide the stories you have finished reading (saved on your own device). A slider moves through time and shows who was alive at each event (the Hijra, Badr, Uhud, the Trench, Hudaybiyyah, the conquest of Makkah, Yarmouk, Qadisiyyah and more) and roughly how old they were.
- Tap a Companion to read their story translated from the book صور من حياة الصحابة (Images from the Lives of the Companions) by Dr Abd al-Rahman Ra'fat al-Basha (الدكتور عبد الرحمن رأفت الباشا), with a "Little ones" version for children and a "Grown-ups" version, a word to learn in each scene, lessons, a short quiz and a put-it-in-order game. Stories so far: Zayd ibn Harithah, Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Talhah ibn Ubaydullah, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Sa'id ibn Zayd, Abdullah ibn Jahsh, Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, Asma bint Abi Bakr, Umm Salamah, Umm Habibah, Abdullah ibn Abbas, Mu'adh ibn Jabal, Zayd ibn Thabit, Salman al-Farisi, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, Abu Hurayrah, al-Tufayl ibn Amr ad-Dawsi, Thumamah ibn Uthal, Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, Suhayb ar-Rumi, Abu ad-Darda, Usamah ibn Zayd, Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, Abdullah ibn Salam, Suraqah ibn Malik, Abdullah ibn Hudhafah, Umayr ibn Wahb, al-Bara ibn Malik, Amr ibn al-Jamuh, Adi ibn Hatim, Abu Talhah al-Ansari, Hakim ibn Hizam, Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b, Safiyyah bint Abd al-Muttalib, Thabit ibn Qays, Sa'id ibn Amir al-Jumahi, Zayd al-Khayr, Majza'ah ibn Thawr, Usayd ibn Hudayr, al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin, Umayr ibn Sa'd, Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith, Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, Habib ibn Zayd al-Ansari, Wahshi ibn Harb, Abbad ibn Bishr, Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi', Asim ibn Thabit, Utbah ibn Ghazwan, Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud, Fayruz al-Daylami, Salamah ibn Qays al-Ashja'i, and, from Abdul Wahid Hamid's English book Companions of the Prophet: Abdullah ibn Umar, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Aishah bint Abi Bakr, an-Nu'ayman ibn Amr, Barakah (Umm Ayman), Fatimah bint Muhammad, Julaybib, Muhammad ibn Maslamah, Mus'ab ibn Umayr, Umm Sulaym (Rumaysa bint Milhan), Salim mawla of Abu Hudhayfah, Suhayl ibn Amr and Ubayy ibn Ka'b. And from Mahmood Ahmad Ghadanfar's English book Great Women of Islam: Khadijah, Sawdah, Hafsah, Zaynab bint Khuzaymah, Zaynab bint Jahsh, Juwayriyah, Safiyyah bint Huyayy, Maymunah, Sumayyah, Fatimah bint Asad, Umm Ruman, Umm Haram, Umm Ammarah (Nusaybah bint Ka'b), ar-Rubayyi' bint Mu'awwidh, Furay'ah bint Malik, Umm Hisham bint Harithah, Asma bint Yazid, Kabshah bint Rafi' (Umm Sa'd), Umm al-Mundhir and Umm Waraqah. In those stories, the Arabic is shown wherever the words were found in the books of hadith and seerah.
- Type a name in the "Find a Companion" box to jump straight to that Companion.
- Tap the Prophet's line, peace be upon him, for the Seerah told through the Companions: every scene from their stories in which they are with him, in time order, with scenes that follow each other from the same Companion's story on one page, each linking back to that Companion's whole story.
- An ayah (at-Tawbah 9:100) sits at the top of the page, and the Mothers of the Believers have their own dusty rose line. Majza'ah ibn Thawr, counted by many scholars among the Tabi'een (the next generation), has a dull purple line.
- Dates are approximate.
